```{python}
#| label: setup

import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import os
import sys
from IPython.display import HTML

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join('..', '..'))
from chart_utils import (
    use_slide_chart_defaults, figure_with_shift_toggle, styled_table_with_toggle,
    attach_global_pct_meta, attach_global_period_meta, tickformat_for_range, CHART_CONFIG,
)
use_slide_chart_defaults()

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join('..', '..', '..', 'run_sets', 'shorten-longest-commutes'))
import report_loader as loader

frames = loader.load()
scenario_ids = frames['scenario_ids']
corridor_volumes = frames['corridor_volumes']
freeway_by_county = frames['freeway_by_county']
corridor_orientation = frames['corridor_orientation']
vmt_vhd = frames['vmt_vhd_by_county_facility']
congested_miles = frames['congested_miles']
vht_hh = frames['vht_per_household']
transit = frames['transit_ridership']
trip_length = frames['hbw_trip_length']
trip_length_dist = frames['hbw_trip_length_distribution']

COUNTY_ORDER = ['Salt Lake', 'Davis', 'Utah', 'Weber', 'Box Elder', 'Region']
TRANSIT_LINE_ORDER = ['FrontRunner', 'TRAX Blue Line', 'TRAX Green Line', 'TRAX Red Line', loader.BUS_LABEL]
PERIOD_ORDER = loader.PERIOD_ORDER  # ['Peak', 'Off-Peak', 'Daily']

# No geography-type dimension here (unlike bring-work-trips-closer-to-home)
# -- every chart shows one plain single-color series per county/facility/
# corridor, with the shift-level toggle (chart_utils.figure_with_shift_
# toggle's global_shift=True row, in the deck-wide toggle bar) picking
# which shift level (5%/10%) is showing.
BAR_COLOR = '#2a78d6'
SHIFT_COLORS = {'5%': '#a6cee3', '10%': '#3182bd'}

PRIMARY_SHIFT_PCT = 10

# Two-column slides (::: {.column width="50%"}) need each chart's own
# width override -- see bring-work-trips-closer-to-home/slides.qmd's own
# docstring for why.
HALF_WIDTH = 540
```

## The Question

::: {.incremental}
- What if we trimmed the region's **longest** home-based-work commutes back toward a typical commute length — wherever they are, no target area involved?
- Sketch test: redistribute the longest 5% / 10% of region-wide daily HBW trip volume (selected purely by distance) toward destinations near the region's own median commute distance
- No geography boundary — selection is region-wide, following today's existing destination pattern in that distance band
- 2027 RTP adoption-year network, model v10.0.0-beta.1 — same baseline model run as the companion Bringing Work Trips Closer to Home run set
:::

::: {.notes}
This is a directional, order-of-magnitude check, not a land-use forecast — see the caveats slide. Different mechanism from the companion run set: that one targets a named geography; this one targets trip length, region-wide.
:::

## Big Picture: Both Shift Levels at Once
```{python}
region_shift = vmt_vhd[
    (vmt_vhd['CO_NAME'] == 'Region') & (vmt_vhd['scenario_id'] != loader.BASELINE_SCENARIO)
].groupby(['shift_pct', 'period'], as_index=False)[['delta_DY_VMT', 'base_DY_VMT', 'delta_DY_VHD', 'base_DY_VHD']].sum()
region_shift['pct_DY_VMT'] = region_shift['delta_DY_VMT'] / region_shift['base_DY_VMT'] * 100
region_shift['pct_DY_VHD'] = region_shift['delta_DY_VHD'] / region_shift['base_DY_VHD'] * 100
region_shift['shift_label'] = region_shift['shift_pct'].apply(lambda v: f'{int(v)}%')
shift_label_order = [f'{int(s)}%' for s in sorted(region_shift['shift_pct'].unique())]

def _big_picture_variant(sub, y_col, y_title, suffix):
    fig = px.bar(
        sub, x='shift_label', y=y_col, color='shift_label',
        category_orders={'shift_label': shift_label_order},
        color_discrete_map=SHIFT_COLORS,
        labels={'shift_label': 'Shift', y_col: y_title},
    )
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line_color='#c3c2b7', line_width=1)
    fig.update_layout(showlegend=False)
    for trace in fig.data:
        if trace.hovertemplate:
            trace.hovertemplate = trace.hovertemplate.replace('%{y}', f'%{{y:+,.3r}}{suffix}')
    return fig

# Same deck-wide-toggle wiring pattern as bring-work-trips-closer-to-home/
# slides.qmd's own Big Picture slide -- see that file's docstring for why
# this chart participates in the Period and Value rows without going
# through figure_with_shift_toggle itself (it already shows every shift
# level at once).
def _big_picture(abs_col, pct_col, abs_title, pct_title, title):
    abs_by_period = {
        p: _big_picture_variant(region_shift[region_shift['period'] == p], abs_col, abs_title, '')
        for p in PERIOD_ORDER
    }
    pct_by_period = {
        p: _big_picture_variant(region_shift[region_shift['period'] == p], pct_col, pct_title, '%')
        for p in PERIOD_ORDER
    }

    fig = abs_by_period['Peak']
    attach_global_period_meta(fig, abs_by_period, PERIOD_ORDER, default_period='Peak')

    pct_combined = go.Figure()
    for p in PERIOD_ORDER:
        for trace in pct_by_period[p].data:
            pct_combined.add_trace(trace)

    abs_range, _pct_range = attach_global_pct_meta(fig, fig, pct_combined, abs_title, pct_title)
    fig.update_layout(
        height=420, width=HALF_WIDTH, title=dict(text=title, font_size=14),
        yaxis=dict(tickformat=tickformat_for_range(abs_range), ticksuffix='', range=abs_range),
    )
    return fig
```

## Congestion: Region-Wide VHD
```{python}
#| fig-align: center
vhd_region_df = vmt_vhd[(vmt_vhd['CO_NAME'] == 'Region') & (vmt_vhd['scenario_id'] != loader.BASELINE_SCENARIO)]
vhd_region_df = vhd_region_df.groupby(['shift_pct', 'period'], as_index=False)[['delta_DY_VHD', 'base_DY_VHD']].sum()
vhd_region_df['pct_DY_VHD'] = vhd_region_df['delta_DY_VHD'] / vhd_region_df['base_DY_VHD'] * 100

def _build_vhd_region(sub, y_col='delta_DY_VHD'):
    fig = px.bar(
        sub, x='shift_pct', y=y_col, color_discrete_sequence=[BAR_COLOR],
        labels={'shift_pct': '', y_col: 'Δ VHD (hrs)'},
    )
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line_color='#c3c2b7', line_width=1)
    fig.update_layout(showlegend=False)
    return fig

fig = figure_with_shift_toggle(
    vhd_region_df, _build_vhd_region, pct_col='pct_DY_VHD',
    value_axis_title='Δ VHD (hrs)', pct_axis_title='Δ VHD (%)',
    period_col='period', default_period='Peak', period_order=PERIOD_ORDER,
    global_shift=True, global_period=True, global_pct=True,
)
fig.update_layout(height=460, title=dict(text='Change in Vehicle-Hours of Delay, Region', font_size=15))
fig.show(config=CHART_CONFIG)
```

## Severe Congestion: Miles Over Capacity
```{python}
#| fig-align: center
cm_ft = congested_miles[(congested_miles['CO_NAME'] == 'Region') & (congested_miles['scenario_id'] != loader.BASELINE_SCENARIO)].copy()
cm_base_ft = cm_ft['base_congested_miles']
cm_ft['pct_congested_miles'] = (
    (cm_ft['delta_congested_miles'] / cm_base_ft.where(cm_base_ft > 0, 1) * 100).where(cm_base_ft > 0, 0.0)

    fig.add_hline(y=0, line_color='#c3c2b7', line_width=1)
    fig.update_layout(xaxis_tickangle=-15)

fig = figure_with_shift_toggle(

    value_axis_title='Δ Congested Miles', pct_axis_title='Δ Congested Miles (%)',
```

Miles of roadway with volume/capacity > 1.0 — a length-based capacity read, distinct from delay (VHD), more directly comparable to how funding/capacity-expansion needs are scoped.

## Trip Length Distribution
```{python}
#| fig-align: center
td = trip_length_dist.copy()
td['shift_label'] = td['shift_pct'].apply(lambda v: 'Baseline' if v == 0 else f'{int(v)}%')

def _build_td(sub):
    fig = px.line(
        sub, x='bin_label', y='share_pct', color='shift_label', markers=True,
        category_orders={'bin_label': loader.DISTANCE_BIN_LABELS, 'shift_label': ['Baseline', '5%', '10%']},
        color_discrete_map={'5%': SHIFT_COLORS['5%'], '10%': SHIFT_COLORS['10%'], 'Baseline': '#898781'},
        labels={'bin_label': 'HBW Trip Length', 'share_pct': 'Share of Trips (%)', 'shift_label': 'Scenario'},
    )
    fig.update_traces(selector=dict(name='Baseline'), line=dict(color='black', dash='dash', width=2), marker=dict(color='black'))
    return fig

fig = figure_with_shift_toggle(td, _build_td, always_include=[0], period_col='period', default_period='Peak', period_order=PERIOD_ORDER, global_shift=True, global_period=True)
fig.update_layout(height=460, title=dict(text='HBW Trip Length Distribution, Baseline vs. Shift<br><sup>2-mile bins, Peak/Off-Peak-correct distance</sup>', font_size=15))
fig.update_xaxes(range=[-0.5, loader.DISTANCE_BIN_EDGES.index(30) - 0.5])
fig.update_yaxes(range=[0, 25])
fig.show(config=CHART_CONFIG)
```

The long tail shrinks, the middle (near the region's median commute distance) grows — the mechanism working as intended, region-wide.

## Caveats
:::  {.incremental}
- **Not a real land-use/economic forecast** — no businesses relocate, no zoning changes simulated
- **Feasibility not checked** — model doesn't confirm destinations could absorb the added trips
- **Sketch-level, order-of-magnitude** — trips manually reallocated on today's existing pattern
- **HBW trips only** — other trip purposes untouched
- **No geography boundary at all** — selection is purely by distance, region-wide; unlike the companion run set, no named area is targeted
- **Selection concentrates unevenly** — some origins see no change, others (plausibly the periphery) see a lot
- **Same mechanism at both shift levels** — 5%/10% test sensitivity to size, not to method
:::
